page: Amazon Web Services r6id.large is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor, providing two virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 16 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Storage features include a dedicated 118 GB local NVMe solid-state drive directly attached to the instance, while network capabilities provide a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth without bundled public IPv4 addresses or dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark metrics indicate moderate single-threaded capability alongside constrained aggregate throughput dictated by the two-vCPU hardware footprint. Single-core evaluations show solid mid-tier output, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 1618.0, a stress-ng single-core rating of 1881.78, and a gzip compression throughput of 28.04 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded synthetic metrics place the instance in the lower tier relative to broader cloud offerings, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1855.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2978.2. Memory subsystem evaluations reveal 15.03 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 13.65 GB/sec write bandwidth for large data blocks, complemented by Redis SET throughput reaching 1.92 million operations per second.

From an efficiency perspective, the r6id.large represents an economical entry point for applications requiring substantial memory allocation per compute thread along with high-speed local disk persistence, avoiding the expense of higher-core configurations. However, workloads requiring intensive multi-threaded compute or significant network bandwidth face physical ceilings on this size. The configuration is best aligned with memory-intensive workloads that require low-latency scratch storage, such as distributed cache nodes, Redis deployments, temporary database staging, batch data extraction, and lightweight in-memory data processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r6id.large is a memory-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro system, designed for applications requiring high memory density per compute unit. The instance features two vCPUs across one physical core from a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor, supported by 16 GB of DDR4 RAM and 118 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. The network interface supports a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth, with no integrated GPU hardware. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits competitive single-core execution speeds, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1618.0 and a compression rate of 28.04 GB/sec, though overall multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit. Memory write and read bandwidth hover around 14 to 15 GB/sec on large data blocks, supporting up to 1.92 million Redis SET operations per second. This profile offers balanced economics for memory-heavy, localized tasks such as caching layers, Redis instances, and temporary database staging.
